# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction enrichment logic.

FROM python:3.9.2

COPY . /transaction-enrichment-python/

EXPOSE 9898

setup(
    name='categorizationapp',
    packages=['categorizationapp'],
    include_package_data=True,
    install_requires=[
        'Flask==1.1.2',
        'pandas==1.2.4',
        'python-Levenshtein==0.12.2',
        'fuzzywuzzy==0.18.0',
        'gunicorn==20.1.0',
        'scipy==1.7.3',
        'scikit-learn==1.0.1',
        'matplotlib==3.5.1',
        'itsdangerous==2.0.1',
        'Jinja2<3.1.0',
        'Werkzeug<2.1.0'
    ],
)import time
from flask import Flask, g
import logging
import warnings
import pandas as pd

app = Flask(__name__)

# ignore all caught warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

app.logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

# to capture the start time of request
@app.before_request
def before_request():
    g.start = time.time()

# to calculate total time taken for request-respone
@app.after_request
def after_request(response):
    diff = time.time() - g.start
    app.logger.info(f"Total time taken : {diff}s")
    return response

pd.set_option('display.max_rows', None)

import categorizationapp.Controller

steps.message:
All bank scripts run cleanly. Summary of the five faults found and fixed (all deterministic, single-row reproducible, on edge shapes):

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py`**

1. **Line 100 — cheque deposit from an all-numeric reference note (`mango_saver`, part 1).** The rule required `remark` length `15` while its own regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 characters, so the condition could never be true and the row fell through to the default `TRANSFER`. HDFC reference notes are a 16-char field elsewhere in the same file (`^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$`), so the length check is now `eq(16)` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` again.

2. **Line 124 — salary sub-tag for a bare numeric narration (`mango_saver`, part 2).** Guard compared `accountType == "SAVINGS"`; the account-type enum used everywhere (Controller, `Purpose.py`, other bank scripts) is `"SAVING"`, so the rule was dead. Now `"SAVING"` → `SALARY` sub-tag restored for `^[0-9]{6}$` credits.

3. **Line 98 — offsetting credit recorded as bounce instead of reversal (maintainer note).** The reversal rule compared the description against `shift(periods=2)` (two rows back) while matching type/amount against the immediately preceding row, so the matching pair fell through to the next rule (`AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`). Changed to `shift(periods=1)`, matching the identical rules in `ICICI.py:49` and `Saraswat.py:20`.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py`**

4. **Line 147 — slash-delimited bill transfer payee (`auditlens`).** For `BIL/INFT/<numeric ref>/<payee>` (four fields, `count("/") == 3`) the extractor took field index 2 (the numeric reference) instead of the final field. Now `sep_by_(description, 3, 4)`, consistent with the sibling `INF/INFT` rule on line 154.

5. **Line 159 — leading direction keyword swallowing the counterparty (`rk_ontheroad`).** `py_extract(..., pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned the first capture group — the direction word itself — so names came back as `"From"` or were wiped to empty. Index changed to `1` (the name group), matching the convention used at line 168 and in `SBI.py`.

I verified with a differential run over ~60 synthetic HDFC/ICICI narrations across `SAVING`/`CURRENT`: the only output changes are the reported edge shapes (`CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` for the numeric reference note, `SALARY` for the bare numeric narration, `REVERSAL` for the offsetting credit, and correct payee names for `TRFR TO:/FROM:` and `BIL/INFT/…`). One knock-on: a numeric-reference cheque credit whose narration is only a plain name no longer gets that name copied into `partyName`, because that copy rule is gated on the `TRANSFER` category — inherent to the rule precedence being restored, not a separate regression.
